title: Yuri Grigorovich’s ballets made the Bolshoi’s name. Now the theater may have to pay his assistant for the privilege of dancing them.
text: stories Yuri Grigorovich’s ballets made the Bolshoi’s name. Now the theater may have to pay his assistant for the privilege of dancing them. August 13, 2026, 8:12 pm Source: Meduza Swan Lake performed by the Bolshoi Theater ballet company Robbie Jack / Corbis / Getty Images Shortly before he died, the renowned choreographer Yuri Grigorovich gave his assistant, Ruslan Pronin, the copyright to 11 of his productions free of charge, the magazine Post- reported , citing unnamed sources. Meduza has independently confirmed the report. Grigorovich died on May 19, 2025. Several weeks later, on July 3, 2025, Pronin founded a nonprofit called the Yuri Grigorovich Foundation and transferred all rights to the foundation’s name. He then demanded that all theaters in Russia and abroad staging Grigorovich’s ballets pay royalties to the foundation — in the Bolshoi Theater’s case, about 1 million rubles per performance. The 11 productions include Grigorovich’s revised versions of classical ballets, among them Swan Lake and Giselle , as well as original ballets of his own, such as Spartacus and Ivan the Terrible . title: Russians will be able to buy cemetery plots through Gosuslugi government services portal
text: Russia’s Gosuslugi government services portal will launch a tool for searching for and purchasing cemetery plots, backed by 295.5 million rubles in funding, the Russian business daily Kommersant reported after reviewing documents from the Digital Development Ministry. The service is set to launch in 21 regions by December 1, 2026, once information on 14,000 cemeteries has been uploaded to the National System of Spatial Data ( NSPD ), roughly a fifth of all cemeteries in Russia, according to the newspaper’s calculations. The Digital Development Ministry stated that the project is currently being piloted in six regions and that a full rollout would bring more transparency to the funeral business. Alexey Suloyev, president of the Association of Crematoriums of Russia, told the newspaper he agreed the system could help reduce corruption in how burial plots are allocated. But he said several familiar problems had already surfaced during the pilot phase: data uploads from state registries weren’t seamless, digital records on burial sites were fragmented, and the interactive map sometimes failed to let users select a plot. title: Putin visits the Kuril Islands for the first time. Japan issues a strong protest.
text: Russian President Vladimir Putin made his first trip to the Kuril Islands, traveling to the island of Iturup, the Kremlin’s press service reported. During the trip, Putin visited the Yasny fish processing plant, the Kuril Central District Hospital, and a school named after Hero of Russia E.D. Norpolov, and met with Sakhalin region Governor Valery Limarenko. Limarenko told Putin that at meetings with residents — even in the most remote places — “the population says: everything for victory.” “That’s the kind of people we have. The genetic code of a winner,” Putin replied, according to the Russian state news agency TASS. Japan’s Foreign Ministry issued a message saying the country “strongly protests” over Putin’s visit to the Kurils, Kyodo News reported . Speaking a day earlier at Pacific Fleet exercises, Putin said Russia had maintained a constructive relationship over the Kuril Islands with former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe and other Japanese leaders — but that Tokyo has since changed its position. title: Zelensky: 5% of U.S. interceptor missiles would get Ukraine through the winter; 10% would stop all Russian ballistic missiles
text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said in an interview with CNN that Ukraine is receiving two and a half times fewer interceptor missiles this year than it did in 2025, even as Russia has doubled the number of ballistic missiles it launches each month. Likely referring to U.S. stockpiles, Zelensky said that if the U.S. would “sell us 5%, we will go through the winter and save people’s lives. If they can sell us 10%, we will destroy all the Russians’ ballistic missiles. I have 1%.” He added: This is what I live each day: from 1% to 5%. I have some months, and million phone calls … I try to exchange something to missiles … I do some things which I can’t even share. It doesn’t mean that it’s outside of the law. But I can’t speak about it. Patriot missile systems are critical to Ukraine’s air defenses amid Russia’s regular strikes, and Zelensky has repeatedly pressed allies for new missile shipments. In early August, he said that Ukraine had run out of interceptor missiles for its Patriot systems. title: Fire at oil refinery and Wildberries warehouse reported following Ukrainian attack on Russia’s Bashkortostan
text: Ukraine attacked Russia’s Republic of Bashkortostan with drones. Radiy Khabirov, the region’s governor, said “drone debris” fell in an industrial zone in the city of Salavat, sparking a fire. No deaths or injuries have been reported so far. Ukrainian Telegram channels Supernova+ and Exilenova+ claimed the strike hit an oil refinery in Salavat. The independent Telegram channel Astra reported that residents saw smoke rising from the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat plant, one of Russia’s largest oil refineries. Ukrainian channels also reported that the drone attack sparked a fire at a Wildberries warehouse. Local media wrote that residents of the Chishminsky district in Bashkortostan saw black smoke near the company’s distribution center. Neither Wildberries nor local authorities have commented publicly. Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat was attacked previously, overnight on July 14. The following day, Reuters sources reported that the strike had damaged two primary oil-processing units at the plant, forcing them offline. title: Fires, Floods and Foul Air: In Siberia’s Tyumen Region, Weather Disasters Turn Biblical
text: Fires, Floods and Foul Air: In Siberia’s Tyumen Region, Weather Disasters Turn Biblical By Leyla Latypova Aug. 13, 2026 A mass fish death in Tyumen's Ozero Krugloye. SOTAvision / Telegram Tyumen, one of Siberia’s largest cities, made national headlines in July when flooding along the local Tura River began to resemble scenes of a biblical plague. Unusually heavy rain fell nearly every day in June and July, pushing the river to 8.96 meters (29.4 feet) by early August, just below the 9.15-meter record set in 1979. As the water rose, local residents complained of an unbearable stench coming from the river and reported seeing scores of dead fish washed ashore. “I suffocate every night and have to shut the windows,” Tyumen resident Svetlana told the Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty news agency. “[Once] I ran out to the street at 1 a.m. looking for a place to breathe. I live across the river and the smell here is worse than anywhere else [in the city],” she told the outlet in July, when daytime temperatures in Tyumen soared to a record-breaking 30 degrees Celsius. “I found some air downtown, away from the river, where I sat on a bench and walked to catch my breath.” A worker involved in c

title: Moscow Universities See Record Admissions Competition Amid Wartime Quotas and Budget Cuts
text: Moscow Universities See Record Admissions Competition Amid Wartime Quotas and Budget Cuts Aug. 13, 2026 The Plekhanov Russian University of Economics. Arthur Novosiltsev / Moskva News Agency High school graduates will face higher competition for tuition-free university spots in Moscow this academic year, state media reported Thursday, as paid seats are being eliminated while military quotas expand. According to data compiled by the state-run TASS news agency, competition for so-called “budget spots” rose by double digits across major institutions including Moscow State University, the Higher School of Economics and the Russian State University for the Humanities. Up to 257 applications per spot were recorded for International Relations at the Plekhanov Russian University of Economics, while the average spot at the university had 34 applications. MSU saw total applications for budget spots jump 46% to more than 91,000. HSE saw an average of 44 applicants per budget spot this admissions cycle, up from 32 last year. Average competition at the Russian State University for the Humanities grew 22% to 167 applications per spot. news 'It's Like Winning at Roulette': War Quotas Squeeze Russ

title: Novosibirsk Activist Who Documented Farmer Protests Arrested on Terrorism Charges
text: Novosibirsk Activist Who Documented Farmer Protests Arrested on Terrorism Charges Aug. 13, 2026 Telegram Authorities in Siberia’s Novosibirsk region have arrested an activist who documented rare local farmer protests this year on charges of calling for terrorism online, her supporters said Thursday. Armed officers raided the home of Larisa Mikhailova, using power tools to cut through the activist’s front door before taking her into custody, her daughter said in a video published by the activist group Agrarian Council. Mikhailova is an activist with the Agrarian Council, which documented cattle culls in the Novosibirsk region mandated by the regional administration. Local farmers accused the authorities of secrecy and failing to adequately compensate them for their slaughtered livestock. Novosibirsk’s Tsentralny District Court later put Mikhailova in pre-trial detention for two months. “I believe this is payback for my mother’s active civic stance,” Mikhailova’s daughter said in the Agrarian Council video. title: Orsk Refinery Shutters for 6 Months After Ukrainian Attack
text: Orsk Refinery Shutters for 6 Months After Ukrainian Attack Aug. 13, 2026 @exilenova_plus / Telegram A major Russian oil refinery in the city of Orsk near the border with Kazakhstan has shut down for up to half a year following a Ukrainian drone attack earlier this week, authorities said Thursday. The Ukrainian military said Tuesday it had attacked the Orsknefteorgsintez refinery, located around 1,500 kilometers (930 miles) from the border with Ukraine. The refinery has an annual processing capacity of 6.6 million metric tons. “The plant has completely shut down,” said Orenburg region Governor Yevgeny Solntsev. He noted that repairs could take up to six months because shrapnel damaged “key infrastructure” that cannot be repaired due to Western sanctions on imported equipment. “We’re preparing for a worst-case scenario and will have to rely on fuel supplies brought in from outside the region,” Solntsev wrote on Telegram. title: Russian Military Officer Killed in Annexed Crimea Bomb Explosion
text: Russian Military Officer Killed in Annexed Crimea Bomb Explosion Aug. 13, 2026 crimea-news.com A senior Russian military officer was killed in a targeted bombing in annexed Crimea, Kremlin-installed officials and the Federal Security Service (FSB) said Thursday. The explosion occurred around 10 a.m. local time on a street in western Sevastopol, the home port of Russia’s Black Sea Fleet, according to the news outlet Ostorozhno Novosti. Citing the FSB, the outlet reported that an explosive device was placed in a trash can and detonated when the officer walked by. The FSB confirmed the death of a Russian Defense Ministry serviceman but did not disclose his identity, according to state news agencies. title: Putin Makes First Visit to Disputed Kuril Islands Amid Protests From Japan
text: Putin Makes First Visit to Disputed Kuril Islands Amid Protests From Japan By AFP Aug. 13, 2026 Vladimir Putin meets residents as he visits the Southern Kuril Island of Iturup. Sputnik / Gavriil Grigorov / Pool via REUTERS President Vladimir Putin visited Russia's far-eastern Kuril Islands for the first time on Thursday, prompting protests by Japan, which also claims the territory. Russian-Japanese relations have long been dogged by the contested islands, known in Japan as the Northern Territories and seized by the Soviet Union in 1945. The Kremlin posted a video of Putin on one of the four main islands of the Kurils, with Russian media reporting that he visited a fish-processing plant and was given caviar. "The Northern Territories are an inherent part of Japan's territory, both historically and under international law," Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi told reporters. title: Moscow Court Upholds Visiting Businessman’s Treason Arrest Over Ukrainian Tax Payments, Mediazona Reports
text: Moscow Court Upholds Visiting Businessman’s Treason Arrest Over Ukrainian Tax Payments, Mediazona Reports Aug. 13, 2026 Arthur Novosiltsev / Moskva News Agency A Moscow judge has upheld the pre-trial detention of a 60-year-old businessman accused of state treason for paying taxes in Ukraine, the exiled outlet Mediazona reported Wednesday. Oleg Varyukhin, a former pilot who ran a perfume business in Ukraine, was reportedly arrested in early May after flying into Moscow from Moldova to visit relatives. Russian investigators allege that Varyukhin committed treason by paying mandatory taxes as an individual entrepreneur on his earnings into the Ukrainian state budget. “Every worker in any country is obligated to pay taxes. They have no control over that,” defense attorney Yury Shel told Mediazona. “[Varyukhin] had no say over how the government distributed those tax revenues, just like anyone in any other country,” Shel said. Mediazona reported that Varyukhin was last issued a passport in Russia in 1981 and has never obtained Russian or Ukrainian passports after the collapse of the Soviet Union. title: Ukrainian Drones Attack Wildberries Hub and Oil Refinery in Bashkortostan
text: Ukrainian Drones Attack Wildberries Hub and Oil Refinery in Bashkortostan Aug. 13, 2026 @exilenova_plus / Telegram Ukrainian drones targeted a logistics hub owned by Wildberries and caused a fire at one of Russia’s largest oil refineries in the republic of Bashkortostan Thursday, according to regional officials and exiled news outlets. Regional head Radiy Khabirov said 16 drones were shot down over the city of Salavat and five others over the nearby Chishminsky district. They are located around 1,200 kilometers (745 miles) east of Moscow and more than 1,300 kilometers (808 miles) from the Ukrainian border. “Two people were injured in today’s attacks. title: ‘Absolutely unacceptable’: Japan condemns visit by Vladimir Putin to disputed Kuril Islands
text: Vladimir Putin at a fish processing plant on the disputed Kuril Islands. Photograph: Gavriil Grigorov/Reuters View image in fullscreen Vladimir Putin at a fish processing plant on the disputed Kuril Islands. Photograph: Gavriil Grigorov/Reuters Japan ‘Absolutely unacceptable’: Japan condemns visit by Vladimir Putin to disputed Kuril Islands Japanese PM says islands seized by Soviets late in second world war are part of her country under international law Gavin Blair in Tokyo Thu 13 Aug 2026 08.56 EDT Last modified on Thu 13 Aug 2026 15.40 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The Japanese government has reacted angrily to Vladimir Putin’s first visit to the disputed Kuril Islands, which are claimed by both Tokyo and Moscow. Japan’s foreign minister, Toshimitsu Motegi, summoned the Russian ambassador Nikolay Nozdrev, while the prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, called Putin’s actions “absolutely unacceptable”. Known in Japan as the Northern Territories and by Russia as the Southern Kurils, the islands were seized by the then Soviet Union in the closing stages of the second world war and have been a source of contention ever since. The Soviet Union declared war on Japan in August 1945

title: Trump-led board reportedly votes again to close Kennedy Center for renovations – live
text: 13.08 EDT Trump-led board reportedly votes again to close Kennedy Center for renovations The board of the John F Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts has once again voted to move forward with Donald Trump ’s controversial plan to temporarily close the building for renovations, the New York Times (paywall) is reporting , citing two people with direct knowledge of the proceedings. The decision will be subject to approval by a federal judge. In May, US district judge Christopher Cooper issued a temporary block on Trump’s demand to close the arts institution for two years of renovations, which was due to start in July after the board – mostly handpicked by the president – voted unanimously in favor . But Joyce Beatty , a Democratic US representative of Ohio who sits on the board, sued over the decision. Cooper shut down the plan on the basis that “in ratifying President Trump’s closure announcement, the Board was derelict in discharging the full range of its responsibilities to the Center”. “More specifically, the Board based its decision on an insufficient, one-sided presentation of information and neglected to consider the full range of its statutory obligations and potential adver

text: ТЕ, КТО ДЕРЖАЛ НЕБО РУКАМИ: Жаркий август в Крыму всегда пахнет сухой полынью, соленым морем и раскаленным асфальтом. Но сегодня к этому примешался запах, который ни с чем не спутаешь. Запах оборванного электричества, сгоревшего металла и внезапной, оглушительной тишины. Я смотрю на пронзительно синее крымское небо, и мне кажется, что мы все стали героями какой-то неземной хроники, людьми, которые каждый день пытаются починить свой дом, пока вокруг рушатся привычные миры и созвездия… Железный дождь и тишина Ночью с неба падали злые механические птицы. Они летели, чтобы принести тьму, и город действительно погрузился в темноту. А утром, когда солнце только начинало выжигать росу на траве у электроподстанции, туда пришли они. Пятеро землян. Четверо парней в тяжелых защитных скафандрах МЧС и один тихий человек, чей долг был просто сторожить этот мирный объект. · Антон Чудаков , капитан, за плечами которого были тысячи спасенных жизней. · Александр Панчук , инженер, знавший каждый винтик в этих смертоносных игрушках. · Артём Дуплин , молодой парень, водитель-сапер, у которого впереди была целая жизнь. · Роман Пилипчук , опытный боец, шедший туда, где опаснее всего. · Василий Староверов

title: Moscow Universities See Record Admissions Competition Amid Wartime Quotas and Budget Cuts
text: Moscow Universities See Record Admissions Competition Amid Wartime Quotas and Budget Cuts Aug. 13, 2026 The Plekhanov Russian University of Economics. Arthur Novosiltsev / Moskva News Agency High school graduates will face higher competition for tuition-free university spots in Moscow this academic year, state media reported Thursday, as paid seats are being eliminated while military quotas expand. According to data compiled by the state-run TASS news agency, competition for so-called “budget spots” rose by double digits across major institutions including Moscow State University, the Higher School of Economics and the Russian State University for the Humanities. Up to 257 applications per spot were recorded for International Relations at the Plekhanov Russian University of Economics, while the average spot at the university had 34 applications. MSU saw total applications for budget spots jump 46% to more than 91,000. HSE saw an average of 44 applicants per budget spot this admissions cycle, up from 32 last year. The decision will be subject to approval by a federal judge. In May, US district judge Christopher Cooper issued a temporary block on Trump’s demand to close the arts institution for two years of renovations, which was due to start in July after the board – mostly handpicked by the president – voted unanimously in favor . Arthur Novosiltsev / Moskva News Agency High school graduates will face higher competition for tuition-free university spots in Moscow this academic year, state media reported Thursday, as paid seats are being eliminated while military quotas expand. According to data compiled by the state-run TASS news agency, competition for so-called “budget spots” rose by double digits across major institutions including Moscow State University, the Higher School of Economics and the Russian State University for the Humanities. Up to 257 applications per spot were recorded for International Relations at the Plekhanov Russian University of Economics, while the average spot at the university had 34 applications. text: Orsk Refinery Shutters for 6 Months After Ukrainian Attack Aug. 13, 2026 @exilenova_plus / Telegram A major Russian oil refinery in the city of Orsk near the border with Kazakhstan has shut down for up to half a year following a Ukrainian drone attack earlier this week, authorities said Thursday. Oleg Varyukhin, a former pilot who ran a perfume business in Ukraine, was reportedly arrested in early May after flying into Moscow from Moldova to visit relatives. title: Colombia and Venezuela earthquakes: How the government responses differed | AP News
text: Franklin Fuentes searches for missing relatives in the collapsed building where they lived two days after earthquakes struck La Guaira, Venezuela, June 26, 2026. (AP Photo/Ariana Cubillos, File) By ISABEL DEBRE Leer en español Add AP News on Google Add AP News as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Share Share Facebook Copy Link copied Print Email X LinkedIn Bluesky Flipboard Pinterest Reddit BUENOS AIRES, Argentina (AP) — For the second time in two months, the ground was shaking in South America. Once again, families flooded social media with pleas for help finding missing loved ones under flattened buildings. Once again, governments across political divides and continents pledged aid . But in many ways, the contrast between Colombia’s 7.4-magnitude earthquake on Monday and Venezuela’s back-to-back temblors on June 24 could not have been more stark. In Venezuela, acting President Delcy Rodríguez waited nearly four hours before addressing the nation. In Colombia, newly inaugurated President Abelardo de la Espriella announced an emergency command post to oversee rescue efforts barely an hour after the earthquake struck. title: Moscow Universities See Record Admissions Competition Amid Wartime Quotas and Budget Cuts
text: Moscow Universities See Record Admissions Competition Amid Wartime Quotas and Budget Cuts Aug. 13, 2026 The Plekhanov Russian University of Economics. Arthur Novosiltsev / Moskva News Agency High school graduates will face higher competition for tuition-free university spots in Moscow this academic year, state media reported Thursday, as paid seats are being eliminated while military quotas expand. According to data compiled by the state-run TASS news agency, competition for so-called “budget spots” rose by double digits across major institutions including Moscow State University, the Higher School of Economics and the Russian State University for the Humanities. Up to 257 applications per spot were recorded for International Relations at the Plekhanov Russian University of Economics, while the average spot at the university had 34 applications. MSU saw total applications for budget spots jump 46% to more than 91,000. HSE saw an average of 44 applicants per budget spot this admissions cycle, up from 32 last year. Average competition at the Russian State University for the Humanities grew 22% to 167 applications per spot. news 'It's Like Winning at Roulette': War Quotas Squeeze Russ

title: Novosibirsk Activist Who Documented Farmer Protests Arrested on Terrorism Charges
text: Novosibirsk Activist Who Documented Farmer Protests Arrested on Terrorism Charges Aug. 13, 2026 Telegram Authorities in Siberia’s Novosibirsk region have arrested an activist who documented rare local farmer protests this year on charges of calling for terrorism online, her supporters said Thursday. Armed officers raided the home of Larisa Mikhailova, using power tools to cut through the activist’s front door before taking her into custody, her daughter said in a video published by the activist group Agrarian Council. Mikhailova is an activist with the Agrarian Council, which documented cattle culls in the Novosibirsk region mandated by the regional administration. Local farmers accused the authorities of secrecy and failing to adequately compensate them for their slaughtered livestock. Novosibirsk’s Tsentralny District Court later put Mikhailova in pre-trial detention for two months. “I believe this is payback for my mother’s active civic stance,” Mikhailova’s daughter said in the Agrarian Council video. title: Orsk Refinery Shutters for 6 Months After Ukrainian Attack
text: Orsk Refinery Shutters for 6 Months After Ukrainian Attack Aug. 13, 2026 @exilenova_plus / Telegram A major Russian oil refinery in the city of Orsk near the border with Kazakhstan has shut down for up to half a year following a Ukrainian drone attack earlier this week, authorities said Thursday. The Ukrainian military said Tuesday it had attacked the Orsknefteorgsintez refinery, located around 1,500 kilometers (930 miles) from the border with Ukraine. The refinery has an annual processing capacity of 6.6 million metric tons. “The plant has completely shut down,” said Orenburg region Governor Yevgeny Solntsev. He noted that repairs could take up to six months because shrapnel damaged “key infrastructure” that cannot be repaired due to Western sanctions on imported equipment. “We’re preparing for a worst-case scenario and will have to rely on fuel supplies brought in from outside the region,” Solntsev wrote on Telegram. title: Russian Military Officer Killed in Annexed Crimea Bomb Explosion
text: Russian Military Officer Killed in Annexed Crimea Bomb Explosion Aug. 13, 2026 crimea-news.com A senior Russian military officer was killed in a targeted bombing in annexed Crimea, Kremlin-installed officials and the Federal Security Service (FSB) said Thursday. The explosion occurred around 10 a.m. local time on a street in western Sevastopol, the home port of Russia’s Black Sea Fleet, according to the news outlet Ostorozhno Novosti. Citing the FSB, the outlet reported that an explosive device was placed in a trash can and detonated when the officer walked by. The FSB confirmed the death of a Russian Defense Ministry serviceman but did not disclose his identity, according to state news agencies. title: Putin Makes First Visit to Disputed Kuril Islands Amid Protests From Japan
text: Putin Makes First Visit to Disputed Kuril Islands Amid Protests From Japan By AFP Aug. 13, 2026 Vladimir Putin meets residents as he visits the Southern Kuril Island of Iturup. Sputnik / Gavriil Grigorov / Pool via REUTERS President Vladimir Putin visited Russia's far-eastern Kuril Islands for the first time on Thursday, prompting protests by Japan, which also claims the territory. Russian-Japanese relations have long been dogged by the contested islands, known in Japan as the Northern Territories and seized by the Soviet Union in 1945. The Kremlin posted a video of Putin on one of the four main islands of the Kurils, with Russian media reporting that he visited a fish-processing plant and was given caviar. text: ‼️ На Львівщині поліцейські викрили чоловіка, який систематично ґвалтував неповнолітню прийомну доньку Починаючи із серпня 2025 року, фігурант упродовж майже року неодноразово вчиняв дії сексуального характеру та ґвалтував свою малолітню вихованку. Зловмисник примушував дівчинку, якій на той момент було 14 років, виконувати усі його сексуальні фантазії. Щоб подолати опір дитини, чоловік застосовував до неї фізичне та психологічне насильство: бив, забороняв виходити з дому та спілкуватися з друзями, позбавляв мобільного зв’язку. Крім того, погрожував зґвалтувати її молодшу сестру, яка також виховувалась у цій прийомній сім’ї. Фігуранта викрили оперативники Управління протидії кіберзлочинам у Львівській області спільно із слідчими відділення поліції №2 Стрийського районного управління поліції, за процесуального керівництва Стрийської окружної прокуратури. Слідчі повідомили зловмиснику про підозру у вчиненні злочину, передбаченого ч. 2 ст. 156 (Розбещення неповнолітніх), ч. 3 ст. 153 (Сексуальне насильство) та ч. 3 ст.152 (Зґвалтування) Кримінального кодексу України. 👮 Facebook | X | Instagram | TikTok

title: Moscow Court Upholds Visiting Businessman’s Treason Arrest Over Ukrainian Tax Payments, Mediazona Reports
text: Moscow Court Upholds Visiting Businessman’s Treason Arrest Over Ukrainian Tax Payments, Mediazona Reports Aug. 13, 2026 Arthur Novosiltsev / Moskva News Agency A Moscow judge has upheld the pre-trial detention of a 60-year-old businessman accused of state treason for paying taxes in Ukraine, the exiled outlet Mediazona reported Wednesday. Oleg Varyukhin, a former pilot who ran a perfume business in Ukraine, was reportedly arrested in early May after flying into Moscow from Moldova to visit relatives. Russian investigators allege that Varyukhin committed treason by paying mandatory taxes as an individual entrepreneur on his earnings into the Ukrainian state budget. “Every worker in any country is obligated to pay taxes. They have no control over that,” defense attorney Yury Shel told Mediazona. “[Varyukhin] had no say over how the government distributed those tax revenues, just like anyone in any other country,” Shel said. Mediazona reported that Varyukhin was last issued a passport in Russia in 1981 and has never obtained Russian or Ukrainian passports after the collapse of the Soviet Union. title: Ukrainian Drones Attack Wildberries Hub and Oil Refinery in Bashkortostan
text: Ukrainian Drones Attack Wildberries Hub and Oil Refinery in Bashkortostan Aug. 13, 2026 @exilenova_plus / Telegram Ukrainian drones targeted a logistics hub owned by Wildberries and caused a fire at one of Russia’s largest oil refineries in the republic of Bashkortostan Thursday, according to regional officials and exiled news outlets. Regional head Radiy Khabirov said 16 drones were shot down over the city of Salavat and five others over the nearby Chishminsky district. They are located around 1,200 kilometers (745 miles) east of Moscow and more than 1,300 kilometers (808 miles) from the Ukrainian border. “Two people were injured in today’s attacks. Both are in hospitals receiving all necessary care,” he wrote on Telegram. Khabirov said falling debris sparked a fire in an “industrial area.” Exiled media outlet Astra identified the site as the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat refinery, which accounts for 2.7% of Russia’s total refining throughput and which halted operations after being damaged in an attack last month. title: Moscow Universities See Record Admissions Competition Amid Wartime Quotas and Budget Cuts
text: Moscow Universities See Record Admissions Competition Amid Wartime Quotas and Budget Cuts Aug. 13, 2026 The Plekhanov Russian University of Economics. Arthur Novosiltsev / Moskva News Agency High school graduates will face higher competition for tuition-free university spots in Moscow this academic year, state media reported Thursday, as paid seats are being eliminated while military quotas expand. According to data compiled by the state-run TASS news agency, competition for so-called “budget spots” rose by double digits across major institutions including Moscow State University, the Higher School of Economics and the Russian State University for the Humanities. Up to 257 applications per spot were recorded for International Relations at the Plekhanov Russian University of Economics, while the average spot at the university had 34 applications. MSU saw total applications for budget spots jump 46% to more than 91,000. HSE saw an average of 44 applicants per budget spot this admissions cycle, up from 32 last year. Average competition at the Russian State University for the Humanities grew 22% to 167 applications per spot. news 'It's Like Winning at Roulette': War Quotas Squeeze Russ

title: Moscow Universities See Record Admissions Competition Amid Wartime Quotas and Budget Cuts
text: Moscow Universities See Record Admissions Competition Amid Wartime Quotas and Budget Cuts Aug. 13, 2026 The Plekhanov Russian University of Economics. Arthur Novosiltsev / Moskva News Agency High school graduates will face higher competition for tuition-free university spots in Moscow this academic year, state media reported Thursday, as paid seats are being eliminated while military quotas expand. According to data compiled by the state-run TASS news agency, competition for so-called “budget spots” rose by double digits across major institutions including Moscow State University, the Higher School of Economics and the Russian State University for the Humanities. Up to 257 applications per spot were recorded for International Relations at the Plekhanov Russian University of Economics, while the average spot at the university had 34 applications. MSU saw total applications for budget spots jump 46% to more than 91,000. HSE saw an average of 44 applicants per budget spot this admissions cycle, up from 32 last year. Average competition at the Russian State University for the Humanities grew 22% to 167 applications per spot. news 'It's Like Winning at Roulette': War Quotas Squeeze Russ

title: Novosibirsk Activist Who Documented Farmer Protests Arrested on Terrorism Charges
text: Novosibirsk Activist Who Documented Farmer Protests Arrested on Terrorism Charges Aug. 13, 2026 Telegram Authorities in Siberia’s Novosibirsk region have arrested an activist who documented rare local farmer protests this year on charges of calling for terrorism online, her supporters said Thursday. Armed officers raided the home of Larisa Mikhailova, using power tools to cut through the activist’s front door before taking her into custody, her daughter said in a video published by the activist group Agrarian Council. Mikhailova is an activist with the Agrarian Council, which documented cattle culls in the Novosibirsk region mandated by the regional administration. Local farmers accused the authorities of secrecy and failing to adequately compensate them for their slaughtered livestock. title: Orsk Refinery Shutters for 6 Months After Ukrainian Attack
text: Orsk Refinery Shutters for 6 Months After Ukrainian Attack Aug. 13, 2026 @exilenova_plus / Telegram A major Russian oil refinery in the city of Orsk near the border with Kazakhstan has shut down for up to half a year following a Ukrainian drone attack earlier this week, authorities said Thursday. The Ukrainian military said Tuesday it had attacked the Orsknefteorgsintez refinery, located around 1,500 kilometers (930 miles) from the border with Ukraine. The refinery has an annual processing capacity of 6.6 million metric tons. “The plant has completely shut down,” said Orenburg region Governor Yevgeny Solntsev. text: Russian Military Officer Killed in Annexed Crimea Bomb Explosion Aug. 13, 2026 crimea-news.com A senior Russian military officer was killed in a targeted bombing in annexed Crimea, Kremlin-installed officials and the Federal Security Service (FSB) said Thursday. title: Major Russian grain export terminals hit in Ukraine Black Sea port attack
text: Major Russian grain export terminals hit in Ukraine Black Sea port attack Image source, Volodymyr Zelensky/Telegram Image caption, The Russian agriculture ministry announced it was working to redirect cargo flows to alternative ports following a barrage of Ukrainian drones By Laura Gozzi Published 12 August 2026 Updated 13 August 2026 A "massive" Ukrainian drone and missile strike on Russia's port of Novorossiysk has damaged two major grain export terminals and hit the last big Russian naval base on the Black Sea, reports say. Three people, including an eight-year-old child, were killed and another 24 injured in the overnight attack, local officials said. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said Kyiv had launched rockets, jet and naval drones in a "unique operation" to strike the Russian base, although he did not mention grain terminals being hit. Ukraine's military later said four Russian warships, including two frigates, were hit. Russia has not commented on the issue. text: Moscow Universities See Record Admissions Competition Amid Wartime Quotas and Budget Cuts Aug. 13, 2026 The Plekhanov Russian University of Economics. Arthur Novosiltsev / Moskva News Agency High school graduates will face higher competition for tuition-free university spots in Moscow this academic year, state media reported Thursday, as paid seats are being eliminated while military quotas expand. According to data compiled by the state-run TASS news agency, competition for so-called “budget spots” rose by double digits across major institutions including Moscow State University, the Higher School of Economics and the Russian State University for the Humanities. Up to 257 applications per spot were recorded for International Relations at the Plekhanov Russian University of Economics, while the average spot at the university had 34 applications. title: Moscow Universities See Record Admissions Competition Amid Wartime Quotas and Budget Cuts
text: Moscow Universities See Record Admissions Competition Amid Wartime Quotas and Budget Cuts Aug. 13, 2026 The Plekhanov Russian University of Economics. Arthur Novosiltsev / Moskva News Agency High school graduates will face higher competition for tuition-free university spots in Moscow this academic year, state media reported Thursday, as paid seats are being eliminated while military quotas expand. According to data compiled by the state-run TASS news agency, competition for so-called “budget spots” rose by double digits across major institutions including Moscow State University, the Higher School of Economics and the Russian State University for the Humanities. Up to 257 applications per spot were recorded for International Relations at the Plekhanov Russian University of Economics, while the average spot at the university had 34 applications. MSU saw total applications for budget spots jump 46% to more than 91,000. HSE saw an average of 44 applicants per budget spot this admissions cycle, up from 32 last year. Armed officers raided the home of Larisa Mikhailova, using power tools to cut through the activist’s front door before taking her into custody, her daughter said in a video published by the activist group Agrarian Council. Mikhailova is an activist with the Agrarian Council, which documented cattle culls in the Novosibirsk region mandated by the regional administration. Local farmers accused the authorities of secrecy and failing to adequately compensate them for their slaughtered livestock. Novosibirsk’s Tsentralny District Court later put Mikhailova in pre-trial detention for two months. “I believe this is payback for my mother’s active civic stance,” Mikhailova’s daughter said in the Agrarian Council video. title: Orsk Refinery Shutters for 6 Months After Ukrainian Attack
text: Orsk Refinery Shutters for 6 Months After Ukrainian Attack Aug. 13, 2026 @exilenova_plus / Telegram A major Russian oil refinery in the city of Orsk near the border with Kazakhstan has shut down for up to half a year following a Ukrainian drone attack earlier this week, authorities said Thursday. The Ukrainian military said Tuesday it had attacked the Orsknefteorgsintez refinery, located around 1,500 kilometers (930 miles) from the border with Ukraine. The refinery has an annual processing capacity of 6.6 million metric tons. “The plant has completely shut down,” said Orenburg region Governor Yevgeny Solntsev. He noted that repairs could take up to six months because shrapnel damaged “key infrastructure” that cannot be repaired due to Western sanctions on imported equipment. “We’re preparing for a worst-case scenario and will have to rely on fuel supplies brought in from outside the region,” Solntsev wrote on Telegram. title: Russian Military Officer Killed in Annexed Crimea Bomb Explosion
text: Russian Military Officer Killed in Annexed Crimea Bomb Explosion Aug. 13, 2026 crimea-news.com A senior Russian military officer was killed in a targeted bombing in annexed Crimea, Kremlin-installed officials and the Federal Security Service (FSB) said Thursday. The explosion occurred around 10 a.m. local time on a street in western Sevastopol, the home port of Russia’s Black Sea Fleet, according to the news outlet Ostorozhno Novosti. Citing the FSB, the outlet reported that an explosive device was placed in a trash can and detonated when the officer walked by. The FSB confirmed the death of a Russian Defense Ministry serviceman but did not disclose his identity, according to state news agencies. The security agency announced the arrest of a 32-year-old Russian woman who they said was acting on the instructions of Ukrainian special services. “Investigators established that she acted on instructions from Ukrainian special services and showed no remorse,” said Mikhail Razvozhayev, the Kremlin-installed governor of Sevastopol. news Russian Soldier in Crimea Shoots and Kills Fellow Serviceman and 3 Civilians Read more Unverified reporting by Ostorozhno Novosti claimed to identify her a

title: Putin Makes First Visit to Disputed Kuril Islands Amid Protests From Japan
text: Putin Makes First Visit to Disputed Kuril Islands Amid Protests From Japan By AFP Aug. 13, 2026 Vladimir Putin meets residents as he visits the Southern Kuril Island of Iturup. Sputnik / Gavriil Grigorov / Pool via REUTERS President Vladimir Putin visited Russia's far-eastern Kuril Islands for the first time on Thursday, prompting protests by Japan, which also claims the territory. Russian-Japanese relations have long been dogged by the contested islands, known in Japan as the Northern Territories and seized by the Soviet Union in 1945. title: Moscow Court Upholds Visiting Businessman’s Treason Arrest Over Ukrainian Tax Payments, Mediazona Reports
text: Moscow Court Upholds Visiting Businessman’s Treason Arrest Over Ukrainian Tax Payments, Mediazona Reports Aug. 13, 2026 Arthur Novosiltsev / Moskva News Agency A Moscow judge has upheld the pre-trial detention of a 60-year-old businessman accused of state treason for paying taxes in Ukraine, the exiled outlet Mediazona reported Wednesday. Oleg Varyukhin, a former pilot who ran a perfume business in Ukraine, was reportedly arrested in early May after flying into Moscow from Moldova to visit relatives. Russian investigators allege that Varyukhin committed treason by paying mandatory taxes as an individual entrepreneur on his earnings into the Ukrainian state budget. “Every worker in any country is obligated to pay taxes. They have no control over that,” defense attorney Yury Shel told Mediazona. “[Varyukhin] had no say over how the government distributed those tax revenues, just like anyone in any other country,” Shel said. Mediazona reported that Varyukhin was last issued a passport in Russia in 1981 and has never obtained Russian or Ukrainian passports after the collapse of the Soviet Union. title: Ukrainian Drones Attack Wildberries Hub and Oil Refinery in Bashkortostan
text: Ukrainian Drones Attack Wildberries Hub and Oil Refinery in Bashkortostan Aug. 13, 2026 @exilenova_plus / Telegram Ukrainian drones targeted a logistics hub owned by Wildberries and caused a fire at one of Russia’s largest oil refineries in the republic of Bashkortostan Thursday, according to regional officials and exiled news outlets. Regional head Radiy Khabirov said 16 drones were shot down over the city of Salavat and five others over the nearby Chishminsky district. They are located around 1,200 kilometers (745 miles) east of Moscow and more than 1,300 kilometers (808 miles) from the Ukrainian border. “Two people were injured in today’s attacks. Both are in hospitals receiving all necessary care,” he wrote on Telegram. title: Fires, Floods and Foul Air: In Siberia’s Tyumen Region, Weather Disasters Turn Biblical
text: Fires, Floods and Foul Air: In Siberia’s Tyumen Region, Weather Disasters Turn Biblical By Leyla Latypova Aug. 13, 2026 A mass fish death in Tyumen's Ozero Krugloye. SOTAvision / Telegram Tyumen, one of Siberia’s largest cities, made national headlines in July when flooding along the local Tura River began to resemble scenes of a biblical plague. Unusually heavy rain fell nearly every day in June and July, pushing the river to 8.96 meters (29.4 feet) by early August, just below the 9.15-meter record set in 1979. As the water rose, local residents complained of an unbearable stench coming from the river and reported seeing scores of dead fish washed ashore. “I suffocate every night and have to shut the windows,” Tyumen resident Svetlana told the Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty news agency. “[Once] I ran out to the street at 1 a.m. looking for a place to breathe. I live across the river and the smell here is worse than anywhere else [in the city],” she told the outlet in July, when daytime temperatures in Tyumen soared to a record-breaking 30 degrees Celsius. “I found some air downtown, away from the river, where I sat on a bench and walked to catch my breath.” A worker involved in c

title: Moscow Universities See Record Admissions Competition Amid Wartime Quotas and Budget Cuts
text: Moscow Universities See Record Admissions Competition Amid Wartime Quotas and Budget Cuts Aug. 13, 2026 The Plekhanov Russian University of Economics. Arthur Novosiltsev / Moskva News Agency High school graduates will face higher competition for tuition-free university spots in Moscow this academic year, state media reported Thursday, as paid seats are being eliminated while military quotas expand. According to data compiled by the state-run TASS news agency, competition for so-called “budget spots” rose by double digits across major institutions including Moscow State University, the Higher School of Economics and the Russian State University for the Humanities. Up to 257 applications per spot were recorded for International Relations at the Plekhanov Russian University of Economics, while the average spot at the university had 34 applications. MSU saw total applications for budget spots jump 46% to more than 91,000. HSE saw an average of 44 applicants per budget spot this admissions cycle, up from 32 last year. Average competition at the Russian State University for the Humanities grew 22% to 167 applications per spot. news 'It's Like Winning at Roulette': War Quotas Squeeze Russ

title: European drought shrivels crops despite farmers’ best efforts to adapt
text: Advertising European drought shrivels crops despite farmers’ best efforts to adapt Europe The drought roasting much of Europe this summer is taking a heavy toll on crops across the continent, from potatoes in the Netherlands to corn in Bosnia. Triodos, a Dutch bank with a focus on sustainability, has warned that this could reduce gross domestic product across the EU by 1 percent for 2026 – or around €180 billion. title: Moscow Universities See Record Admissions Competition Amid Wartime Quotas and Budget Cuts
text: Moscow Universities See Record Admissions Competition Amid Wartime Quotas and Budget Cuts Aug. 13, 2026 The Plekhanov Russian University of Economics. Arthur Novosiltsev / Moskva News Agency High school graduates will face higher competition for tuition-free university spots in Moscow this academic year, state media reported Thursday, as paid seats are being eliminated while military quotas expand. According to data compiled by the state-run TASS news agency, competition for so-called “budget spots” rose by double digits across major institutions including Moscow State University, the Higher School of Economics and the Russian State University for the Humanities. Up to 257 applications per spot were recorded for International Relations at the Plekhanov Russian University of Economics, while the average spot at the university had 34 applications. MSU saw total applications for budget spots jump 46% to more than 91,000. HSE saw an average of 44 applicants per budget spot this admissions cycle, up from 32 last year. title: Orsk Refinery Shutters for 6 Months After Ukrainian Attack
text: Orsk Refinery Shutters for 6 Months After Ukrainian Attack Aug. 13, 2026 @exilenova_plus / Telegram A major Russian oil refinery in the city of Orsk near the border with Kazakhstan has shut down for up to half a year following a Ukrainian drone attack earlier this week, authorities said Thursday. The Ukrainian military said Tuesday it had attacked the Orsknefteorgsintez refinery, located around 1,500 kilometers (930 miles) from the border with Ukraine. The refinery has an annual processing capacity of 6.6 million metric tons. “The plant has completely shut down,” said Orenburg region Governor Yevgeny Solntsev.
